name: Dragon's Blood
lede: Dragon's Blood is a brick red, catalogued by our library as a plant word and first recorded in print in 1599.

sections.title: A resin's name
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, by the account the NBS carried into its 1955 circular, puts the first printed record of the name at 1599, on plate 4 J 10 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system reads the swatch as a moderate red, about 6.2 units from the block center, and Munsell notation gives 7.3R 4.8/8.0 [1]. Our library classes the name with plant words, consistent with the long-standing use of "dragon's blood" for a dark red resin [1].

The nearest named color in our data is [[pompeian-red]], about 3.5 units off, with [[dusty-crimson]], [[reddish-chestnut]] and [[ferruginous]] close behind [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color, as photographed, is common in the archive: 266 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.1 per cent, more common than 72 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It is over-represented in Indian painting, at 69 of 721 works, 3.2 times the overall rate, and further still in the Kalighat school, at 11 of 96 works, 3.1 times expected [3]. Its peak is the 1400s, at 2.9 percent of that century's paintings, 2.3 times the overall rate, and inside a painting it most often plays an accent [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a painting dated 1119, 811 years before the name's 1930 dictionary record, so this is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph had several numbers not supported by data/graph/fieldnotes — the India over-representation (article said 116 of 721, 15x; the real fact is 69 of 721, 3.2x), the Kalighat figure (article said 42 of 96, 41x; the real fact is 11 of 96, 3.1x/4.2x), the invented 'peak decade 1460s' (no matching field; the real peak is the 1400s century fact, 2.9%/2.3x), and the closing sentence, which named a '≈500 CE Maya mural fragment' with no basis (fs.fa is null; the real first-seen record is an unattributed 1119 painting, 811 years before the name's 1930 record — not 'over a thousand years' before 1599). Rewrote the paragraph and the opener/question that repeated the 41x figure from the real country, movement, century, role and first-seen facts. Removed the unsupported numbers rather than inventing replacements.
